Subject: Re: Intro + discovery (POC scope) — short recap and next steps

Hi Samira / Elliot —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of needs
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + triage suggestions for outpatient intake (seq len ~256 typical; up to 1024 worst-case)
- Latency SLA target: 200–300ms p50 for 256 tokens; throughput target: ~120 concurrent inference requests (average 1.5k tokens/minute each)
- Quality sensitivity: hallucination/omission in summaries unacceptable; want >90% fidelity on our internal eval set
- Security: must run in private VPC for PHI — you confirmed Private deployment or Dedicated reserved capacity is required

Initial model guidance (recommended candidates)
- redwood-3-medium (FP16 baseline): best balance quality/latency in our internal eval for clinical summarization
- redwood-3-medium-awq (AWQ-int4): ~1.8–2x throughput vs FP16 with modest degradation on edge cases; good to test for cost savings
- redwood-3-medium-gptq (GPTQ-int4): slightly better quality than AWQ in our lab but more brittle on long-context consistency; useful as a conservative quant alternative
- redwood-3-small-fp8 (FP8 variant): excellent throughput, but higher risk of subtle token-level regressions — only recommend for non-critical paths

What I’m attaching
- stratamed_prompt_set_v1.json (your prompt templates + our canonical eval prompts)
- initial suggested benchmark matrix (CSV) with sequence lengths, batch sizes, and target GPU types
- short writeup: redwood_awq_vs_gptq_tradeoffs.pdf that highlights where AWQ/GPTQ diverge (edge-case safety, small-token hallucination patterns)

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) You confirm the size of the eval set you’ll allow us to run (we suggest 1k clinical notes from your non-production dataset).
2) We run a 48-hour benchmark comparing FP16 / AWQ-int4 / GPTQ-int4 / FP8 on a Dedicated A100 pool with pinned 256/512 seq lengths. Deliverables: accuracy delta vs your eval, per-token latency distribution, cost per 1M tokens estimate.
3) Internal sync (30m) on Wed 12/14 to review preliminary numbers — can Laura or Rishi join for technical follow-up?

Open questions for you
- Can you confirm whether PII/PHI can be used in the non-prod eval cluster under your risk controls?
- Any preferred GPU family for us to benchmark against (A100-v4 / A100-sxm / T4)?

Thanks — I’ll put the benchmark matrix in motion once you confirm the eval set and PHI allowance.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical addendum from the model/quant side: 

Key items to validate in the benchmark matrix
- Sequence length slices: 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024 (we should check both median and tail latencies)
- KV cache warm-start cost: for triage flows that reuse context across turns, AWQ lags slightly on KV caching performance in our tests — measure warm vs cold latency separately
- Sampling settings: use fixed temperature/top_p from your prod templates in stratamed_prompt_set_v1 (we need identical decoding to make quality comparisons fair)

Expected tradeoffs (ballpark numbers from prior POCs)
- AWQ-int4: throughput 1.6–2.2x vs FP16; median latency reduction ~35–55ms for 256 tokens; expected quality delta: 1–3% F1 on strict extraction tests, larger on rare error cases
- GPTQ-int4: throughput 1.4–1.9x vs FP16; tends to preserve exact-token fidelity better than AWQ on our architectures, but depending on kernel selection it can be heavier on memory and slightly less consistent across sequence lengths
- FP8: throughput uplift up to 3x in some backends; quality regression is model-dependent and harder to predict — highly recommended only after acceptance tests pass

Recommended benchmark plan (minimal viable run)
- GPUs: A100-sxm (preferred) and a second run on a cheaper GPU (e.g., T4) to show sensitivity
- Batches: batch sizes 1/4/8 for latency/throughput curve
- Metrics: strict span F1 on your extraction tasks, summary ROUGE-L, hallucination rate (human-labeled sampled subset), p50/p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens

I’ll prepare the benchmark job templates (Docker + run scripts) and share them with Dev for deployment to your Dedicated or Private cluster.

Rishi
